source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

42003.t:
In the governor's race, Allegheny County gave Shapiro 368,577 votes to Garrity's 142,682, a Democratic margin of 44 points. In 2024 Harris beat Trump here by 20, so the county moved 23 points toward the Democrats. That is almost exactly the typical move among Pennsylvania's 67 counties, all of which shifted left, and well above the national typical move of 14 points. Allegheny cast more votes than any other county in the state.

Turnout was 72% of the 2024 vote, with 516,778 ballots against 720,504. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Montgomery, Delaware and Chester, the most similar counties, moved by 22 to 23 points.

42095.t:
Northampton County flipped in the governor's race. Trump carried it by 2 points in 2024; Shapiro won it by 24, taking 78,288 votes to Garrity's 47,252. That is a 26-point move toward the Democrats, slightly more than Pennsylvania's 24-point statewide shift and the typical county's 23, placing it 12th of 67. It was one of 11 Pennsylvania counties to go from Trump to the Democrat. Similar counties moved about as far: Erie 25, Monroe 24 and neighboring Lehigh 27.

Turnout fell sharply. Northampton cast 127,348 votes, 71% of its 2024 total of 178,215, so the count cannot tell voters who switched sides from those who stayed home.

42065.t:
Jefferson County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race but swung sharply toward the Democrats. Garrity carried it 10,072 to 4,720 over Shapiro, a margin of 35 points, down from Trump's 58-point win in 2024. That 23-point move matches the typical Pennsylvania county exactly and places Jefferson 33rd of 67, in a state where every county moved left. Similar counties moved almost identically: Mifflin and Somerset by 23 points each, Juniata by 21.

Turnout fell steeply, to 15,078 votes, about 65% of the 23,129 cast in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from people changing their minds and how much from Republican-leaning voters who stayed home. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

42125.t:
Washington County flipped. Donald Trump carried it by 26 points in 2024, and in the governor's race Democrat Josh Shapiro edged Republican Stacy Garrity here by 2 points, 41,341 votes to 39,363. That is a 28-point move toward the Democrats, sixth-largest of Pennsylvania's 67 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county moved 23 points and the state 24. Washington outpaced its closest comparisons, York (24 points) and Westmoreland (26), both of which stayed narrowly Republican, while Beaver moved 27 and also flipped.

Turnout was far lower than in 2024: 81,888 votes cast, 67% of the presidential total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

42037.t:
Columbia County stayed Republican in the race for Pennsylvania governor but by far less than in 2024. Garrity led Shapiro 11,795 to 10,377, a margin of 6 points, down from Trump's 31-point win here. That is a 25-point move toward the Democrats, slightly more than the statewide shift of 24 points and the typical Pennsylvania county's 23, and well above the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved alike: Mercer by 21 points, Lawrence by 26 and Carbon by 28.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 22,480 votes, 69% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, the figures are close to final.

42081.t:
Lycoming County stayed Republican in the race for governor but by far less than in 2024. Garrity carried it 24,482 to 15,385 over Shapiro, a margin of 23 points, down from Trump's 42-point win. That is a 19-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical Pennsylvania county's 23 points and ranking 57th of 67 in the state, though larger than the typical national move of 14.

Turnout fell sharply: 40,451 votes, 68% of the 2024 total. The count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Blair moved about as much (20 points), while Schuylkill (28) and Cambria (26) moved further.

42097.t:
In the race for governor, Northumberland County voted for Garrity over Shapiro by 15 points, 15,975 to 11,686. In 2024 it backed Trump over Harris by 40 points, so the margin moved 25 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly more than Pennsylvania's statewide swing of 24 points and the typical county's 23. It ranks 20th of 67 counties by size of move, and every county in the state shifted left.

Only 28,185 votes were cast, 65% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar Republican counties moved comparably: Indiana and Cambria by 26 points each, Crawford by 19.

42015.t:
Bradford County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race but by a much smaller margin. Stacy Garrity beat Josh Shapiro 13,651 to 7,050, a 31-point Republican margin, down from Trump's 48-point win in 2024. That is a 17-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical Pennsylvania county's 23-point shift and ranking 64th of 67 in a state where every county moved left. Comparable Republican counties moved further: Perry by 23 points, Snyder by 20 and McKean by 18.

42105.t:
Potter County stayed heavily Republican in the governor's race, with Garrity beating Shapiro 4,510 to 1,594, a margin of 47 points. That was well short of Trump's 62-point margin in 2024, a 16-point move toward the Democrats. Every Pennsylvania county moved left, but Potter moved less than all but one of the state's 67. The typical county moved 23 points, and similar Republican counties such as Juniata, Jefferson and Mifflin moved 21 to 23.

Turnout fell sharply. The 6,227 votes cast were 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who switched sides from those who stayed home.

42005.t:
Armstrong County stayed firmly Republican in the race for governor but moved sharply toward the Democrats. Garrity won it 15,401 to 8,124 over Shapiro, a margin of 30 points, down from Trump's 53-point win in 2024. That 23-point shift matches the typical Pennsylvania county, where all 67 moved left, and is close to similar counties such as Clarion (+23) and Clearfield (+22), ahead of Huntingdon (+18). Statewide, Shapiro won by 22 points, a 24-point swing from 2024.

Only 23,951 votes were cast, 65% of the 37,119 from 2024. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, these figures should hold.

42119.t:
Union County stayed Republican in the race for governor, but only barely. Stacy Garrity beat Josh Shapiro here 7,152 to 6,893, a margin of about 2 points, after Donald Trump carried the county by 23 points over Kamala Harris in 2024. That 22-point swing toward the Democrats is close to Pennsylvania's typical county move of 23 points. Every county in the state moved left, and Union ranks 46th of 67.

Turnout fell sharply, to 14,212 votes, about two-thirds of the 21,188 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who switched from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved about as much: Pike also stayed narrowly Republican, while Montour and Beaver flipped to Shapiro.

42071.t:
Lancaster County flipped in the race for Pennsylvania governor. It went from Trump by 16 points in 2024 to Shapiro by 4 over Garrity, 110,885 votes to 101,368, with 99% of the expected vote counted. That is a 20-point move toward the Democrats. Every Pennsylvania county moved left, and Lancaster's shift was smaller than the typical county's 23 points, ranking 49th of 67, though above the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved further: Berks by 25 points, Cumberland by 24 and Luzerne by 28.

Turnout was 74% of the 2024 vote, 215,211 ballots against 289,257, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

42045.t:
Delaware County moved about 22 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor, going from Harris's 23-point margin in 2024 to a 46-point win for Shapiro over Garrity, 169,689 votes to 62,219. That is slightly less than the typical Pennsylvania county's 23-point shift and the statewide swing of 24, and close to similar suburban neighbors: Montgomery moved 23 points, Chester 22 and Allegheny 23. 42051.t:
Fayette County voted for Garrity over Shapiro in the race for governor, 21,238 to 16,831, a Republican margin of 11 points. 42041.t:
In the race for Pennsylvania governor, Cumberland County backed Shapiro over Garrity by about 15 points, 64,557 votes to 47,879. Trump had carried it by 9 points in 2024, so the county moved 24 points toward the Democrats and flipped, one of 11 Pennsylvania counties to go from a Trump win to a Democratic one. That shift matched the statewide move of 24 points and ranked 25th of 67 counties. Comparable counties moved similarly: Berks by 25 points, Northampton by 26 and Lancaster by 20.

Turnout fell to 114,527 votes, 77% of the 148,396 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Kamala Harris carried it by 6 points in 2024, so the county moved 22 points toward the Democrats, slightly less than the statewide swing of 24 and the typical Pennsylvania county's 23. All 67 counties moved left, and Dauphin ranks 41st.

Turnout was 114,579 votes, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among counties with similar 2024 results, Lehigh moved 27 points and Lackawanna 30, while Centre moved 20.

42101.t:
In the race for Pennsylvania governor, Philadelphia County gave Democrat Shapiro 436,266 votes to Republican Garrity's 49,821, a margin of 79 points. Harris carried the county by 59 points in 2024, so it moved 20 points toward the Democrats. That is a large swing by national standards, where the typical county moved 14 points, but smaller than in most of Pennsylvania. Every county in the state moved left, the typical one by 23 points, and Philadelphia ranks 52nd of 67. Montgomery, Delaware and Allegheny, the most similar counties, each moved 22 to 23 points.

Turnout was 68% of the 2024 level, 490,015 votes against 721,441, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.
